summary: The iterative scanner trims ordinary large literals correctly and passes the acceptance suite, but it reintroduces 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' through `result.push(...trailingSpaces)` whenever a literal has a long run of spaces (~100k+) followed by a non-space or an escaped quote. It also changes behaviour on unbalanced input: an unterminated quote now gets a closing quote added and its trailing spaces dropped, where the old regex left it untouched.

findings.claim: `result.push(...trailingSpaces)` spreads the buffered spaces as call arguments. When a large literal has an internal run of spaces longer than V8's argument limit (~100k), it throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. That is the same failure the task asked to remove. Lines 72-73 have the same problem in the escaped-quote branch. Fix: count the spaces and push ' '.repeat(n), or slice the input instead of copying it char by char.
findings.repro: node -e "import('/work/tools/sql-literals.mjs').then(m=>m.trimLiterals(\"'\"+' '.repeat(200000)+\"x'\"))"  -> RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded

findings.claim: An unterminated literal is closed by force. The old regex only touched matched '...' pairs, so an odd quote count left the text alone. The new code always appends a closing quote and drops the trailing spaces. The task requires that characters outside recognised pairs are preserved, so this changes output for unbalanced fragments, including a lone quote after balanced literals and a trailing escaped-quote ambiguity.

Building the output as an array of 15M single-character strings and joining it is memory-heavy, at ~0.9 s for a 15M literal. Copying slices with sql.slice/indexOf would be simpler and faster, and would avoid the spread bug altogether.
